title: Amiga
summary: Amiga is a family of personal computers produced by Commodore from 1985 until 1994, notable for custom hardware that accelerated graphics and sound. It established a niche in audio and multimedia, becoming a popular platform for music creation and video production. The system's custom chips enabled sprite graphics, blitting, and four channels of sample-based audio, supporting a desktop GUI and pre-emptive multitasking via AmigaOS. While initially slow to sell, the Amiga 500 became the bestselling model, finding success in gaming and creative software before market share declined against IBM PC compatibles and fourth-generation consoles, leading to Commodore's bankruptcy.

mechanisms.title: Custom graphics and blitter
